item.title: Spark Program | secnev — CKB-native risk observatory (1 posts)
item.description: 1. Project overview Project name: secnev One sentence: secnev is an open, CKB-native risk observatory that turns live cells, scripts, pools and protocol state into explainable risk scores for CKB stablecoins, vaults, xUDT/RGB++ tokens and wallets. Positioning: risk intelligence infrastructure + public dashboard + free API + developer tooling. What already exists: a working MVP on CKB mainnet, 10 assets, real cell-level data, live RUSD/USDI market price and liquidity, iCKB exchange rate/backing, organic holder concentration, wallet exposure, real dCKB transaction replay, alerts, dashboard, API and Vercel deployment. item.title: Ckbup: one installer for CKB command-line tools (early progress, feedback welcome) (1 posts)
item.description: Update: ckbup now installs five tools. The second step is merged. ckbup install now covers ckb, fnn and ckb-light-client as well as ckb-debugger and ckb-cli. cargo install --git https://github.com/steven3002/ckbup ckbup install ckb ckbup install fnn ckbup install ckb-light-client What changed: The right build for your machine. Each project names its release files differently, and ckbup reads each scheme. For fnn and ckb-light-client it prefers the portable builds: their standard Linux builds need glibc 2.39 and 2.38, while the portable ones run on glibc 2.34. --portable asks for the portable build where a project publishes one. ckb’s release notes recommend it if you see “illegal...

item.title: Twine testnet beta: help test buying and selling CKB without an exchange (1 posts)
item.description: Update. Twine works with Fiber Studio and Cellula Wallet. Fiber Studio is the desktop app. It runs the official Fiber node on your computer. Cellula Wallet is the other one, in the browser and on Android. It pays over Fiber, and you do not run a node for it. The trade is the same. The buyer makes a Fiber invoice in Fiber Studio or Cellula Wallet and pastes it into Twine. The secret stays in that wallet. The seller pays the hold invoice from their own copy of either wallet. After that, the coins cannot be pulled back early. On release, Twine pays the buyer’s invoice. The CKB arrives in the wallet that made it. The local money still goes from one account to the other.
